subject.title: ci: accept trusted unsigned release merge heads

question: Should Full Release Validation trust an unsigned exact canonical release-branch merge head based on unique merged-PR attribution and the merger's current maintain or admin permission?
rationale: The mechanics are narrowly fail-closed, but substituting current GitHub authorization and attribution for a cryptographic signature is a permanent release security-policy choice that automation cannot make.

options.title: Approve after boundary proof
options.body: Accept the constrained unsigned path after inspectable live acceptance/rejection proof and release-owner review.

options.title: Require signed candidates
options.body: Retain signed-only provenance and change release merge creation so every frozen head carries a valid signature.

recommendation.title: Approve after boundary proof
recommendation.body: Accept the constrained unsigned path after inspectable live acceptance/rejection proof and release-owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current individual ownership trail for frozen release validation and the exact candidate that exposed this policy gap.
